runs.t: Design by Contract specifies preconditions, postconditions, and invariants for components. A contract describes obligations between caller and implementation, including behavior when assumptions are violated.

Document valid inputs and states, guarantees on successful return, and properties that must remain true across operations. Enforce meaningful constraints via types, runtime checks, database constraints, and contract tests at trust boundaries.
A wallet transfer requires a positive amount, valid accounts, and an invariant that recorded debit and credit balance. Define what happens on insufficient funds and ensure the operation is atomic.

Types cannot express every runtime or cross-record invariant. Do not rely on assertions that disappear in production, and avoid overly strict preconditions that make substitutable implementations incompatible.

Specify transfer preconditions, postconditions, invariant and error cases before generating any implementation. Ask the agent for transaction tests covering rollback and concurrency.

items.t: State the expected behavior and at least one failure or edge case before asking an agent to implement anything.
Inspect the boundary conditions and dependency direction, not only the happy-path result.
Demand observable evidence: tests, measured results, or a justified design decision.
